name: Wildair
notes: Tiny natural wine bar with a rotating small-plates menu; go for the beef tartare and uni dip.
happy_hour_info: No formal happy hour, but weekday early seatings (5:30-6:30 PM) are easiest to walk into.

name: Rule of Thirds
notes: Sceney waterfront-adjacent spot with excellent sushi and a DJ later in the night.
happy_hour_info: Mon-Fri 5-6:30 PM: discounted sake flights and select rolls.

name: Cervo's
notes: Airy seafood spot from the Court Street Grocers team; great for a light dinner or oysters at the bar.
happy_hour_info: Daily 4-6 PM: $1.75 oysters and $8 house wine.

name: Cafe Mogador
notes: East Village institution since 1983; the lamb tagine and merguez are standouts, great brunch too.
happy_hour_info: No happy hour; weekday lunch prix-fixe is a good value.

name: Dhamaka
notes: Bold, regional Indian tasting menu-style dishes inside Essex Market; book ahead, it's a destination spot.
happy_hour_info: No happy hour; reservations strongly recommended.

name: Employees Only
notes: Classic speakeasy-style cocktail bar with a late-night kitchen and a psychic reader at the door.
happy_hour_info: Daily 4-7 PM: discounted classic cocktails and snacks.

name: Nom Wah Tea Parlor
notes: NYC's oldest dim sum parlor (est. 1920); the egg rolls and shrimp dumplings are cult favorites.
happy_hour_info: No happy hour; go off-peak (2-4 PM) to skip the line.

name: Lilia
notes: Missy Robbins' handmade pasta destination in a converted auto-body shop; reservations open a month out.
happy_hour_info: No happy hour; walk-in bar seats occasionally available for pasta and wine.

name: Sunday in Brooklyn
notes: Multi-floor spot great for brunch (maple pancakes) and a rooftop bar for evening drinks.
happy_hour_info: Rooftop bar has seasonal weekday drink specials 4-6 PM.
